row.rationale: Accepted runtime pre-bind validation kill: removing ValidateOnStart makes all12 configured URL/endpoint rows across both shipped grpc/fleet hosts and all3 restricted profile spellings fail the genuine typed loopback-refusal assertion at test77. Actual observed and recorded exceptions are from the unchanged post-bind LoopbackListenerVerifier (InvalidOperationException with its bound0.0.0.0 address), not the required OptionsValidationException for AshlarInboundListenerOptions. Both forced-disposal endpoint rows also fail77: observed ObjectDisposedException is tied to the same specific recorded post-bind refusal and is not accepted as pre-bind validation. All8 code-binding refusal controls,8 successful-host/TCP controls, and6 exception-authenticity negative controls pass.
row.key_message_excerpt: Expected genuine typed loopback refusal at77, but no matching OptionsValidationException exists. Actual/recorded post-bind System.InvalidOperationException reports non-loopback http://0.0.0.0:<ephemeral-port>; forced observer sees ObjectDisposedException with that recorded failure.

The intended completed-read assertion at ReadScopeTests:85 expects the joined reported Confidential mark and observes SystemHigh. The real model-export fixture additionally records SystemHighData instead of LevelTooLow in both Secret rows, and its Internal control stops egress_refused instead of empty. row.rationale: Allowing a read frame to observe its own synthetic SystemHigh mark outward is detected by 45 runtime failures. The intended completed-read assertion at ReadScopeTests:85 expects the joined reported Confidential mark and observes SystemHigh. All additional failed rows are corresponding overtaint effects: canonical RAG labels and joins, read-nothing paths, nested/concurrent/late/other-flow reports, caller-filter reads, and post-read agent marks become SystemHigh. The real model-export fixture additionally records SystemHighData instead of LevelTooLow in both Secret rows, and its Internal control stops egress_refused instead of empty. The full failure inventory contains only assertions tied to this overtaint, including the otherwise unrelated detach fixtures whose failure occurs at their final completed caller read.

row.rationale: Suppressing the labelled-tool ReportRead callback is detected by 35 runtime failures. The primary 19 canonical tier variants at TwinTests:256 and all other affected RAG/agent mark assertions observe SystemHigh instead of their reported Public/Internal/Confidential/Secret/TopSecret labels. The no-hit and unrankable-refusal paths likewise lose their Public report. The real model fixtures detect the corresponding SystemHighData denial or premature egress_refused stop. Two additional rows specifically confirm that reporting callbacks were skipped: ReportThenThrowTool stops empty instead of error, and HostileLabelledTool records no Report invocation. All failures therefore concern callback loss or its fail-closed downstream effect.

reviews.rationale: All 26 actual failures are consistent with omitting EgressHttp's follower insertion. The intended async same-host test reaches Twin:70 after status 200 and the two requested paths pass, but records one decision instead of two; synchronous Twin:90 likewise observes one decision. Constructed-primary checks at Hardening:29 and Twin:50 find auto-redirect still enabled. Runtime chain/state checks find the follower absent at HttpHandlerTwin:384, Netstandard20Twin:151/166, Hardening:183/573/600 (including credentialed and unknown-primary callers), and DifferentialHardening:303 via 224. Eight O2 boundary variants at Hardening:399 retain their prior 307 and single-send assertions but lack the attempted-boundary decision. Cross-host and report-P2 tests at Twin:107/127 return 200 instead of 307. The rewriter test at Twin:205 observes evaluation after send, and the relative-URI test at Hardening:500 observes too few pre-send decisions. The intermediate-disposal fixture stops at Hardening:554 because it receives 302 rather than 200. These are runtime pipeline construction, state and behavior failures, including execution of the netstandard2.0 asset; they are not source-convention scans.

row.rationale: All 26 actual failures are consistent with omitting EgressHttp's follower insertion. The intended async same-host test reaches Twin:70 after status 200 and the two requested paths pass, but records one decision instead of two; synchronous Twin:90 likewise observes one decision. Constructed-primary checks at Hardening:29 and Twin:50 find auto-redirect still enabled. Runtime chain/state checks find the follower absent at HttpHandlerTwin:384, Netstandard20Twin:151/166, Hardening:183/573/600 (including credentialed and unknown-primary callers), and DifferentialHardening:303 via 224. Eight O2 boundary variants at Hardening:399 retain their prior 307 and single-send assertions but lack the attempted-boundary decision. Cross-host and report-P2 tests at Twin:107/127 return 200 instead of 307. The rewriter test at Twin:205 observes evaluation after send, and the relative-URI test at Hardening:500 observes too few pre-send decisions. The intermediate-disposal fixture stops at Hardening:554 because it receives 302 rather than 200. These are runtime pipeline construction, state and behavior failures, including execution of the netstandard2.0 asset; they are not source-convention scans.

reviews.rationale: All 33 failures trace to removing the factory filter's primary follower. The intended cross-host factory test at Twin:180, and same-host companion at 155, retain successful status/request assertions but lose the second decision. Real loopback DifferentialHardening:102 observes the second authority's decision after its server hop instead of before. More seriously, the enforcing loopback fixture reaches DifferentialHardening:134 after an EgressRefusedException and two decision records were observed, but the server has already received two requests instead of one: refusal occurred after the forbidden hop. DifferentialHardening:170 leaves the primary's auto-redirect enabled; the controlled-primary enforcement fixture at Hardening:144 gets no expected refusal. Composite, cloned-response, scheme/port, custom-guard, userinfo and boundary fixtures fail respectively on status 307 versus 200 (345/426), missing repeated or rewritten decisions (315/282), and missing attempted-hop decisions (452/477/384/255). Eight shared-primary NeverFollow variants at line 51 plus outer-client line 76, ordinary-client line 93 and Hardening:209 fail the ordinary-follow control with 307 rather than 200 after their restricted-client assertions pass. The unsupported-scheme fixture is the one secondary non-assertion failure: it raises HttpRequestException/SocketException at DifferentialHardening:195/330 while trying files.example:21. Its ConnectCallback explicitly maps every requested host to loopback, so the removed scheme-filtering follower explains an inappropriate local port-21 connection attempt, not an unexplained remote-network outage. Acceptance is independently anchored by the intended decision assertion and the other relevant runtime assertions.

row.rationale: All 33 failures trace to removing the factory filter's primary follower. The intended cross-host factory test at Twin:180, and same-host companion at 155, retain successful status/request assertions but lose the second decision. Real loopback DifferentialHardening:102 observes the second authority's decision after its server hop instead of before. More seriously, the enforcing loopback fixture reaches DifferentialHardening:134 after an EgressRefusedException and two decision records were observed, but the server has already received two requests instead of one: refusal occurred after the forbidden hop. DifferentialHardening:170 leaves the primary's auto-redirect enabled; the controlled-primary enforcement fixture at Hardening:144 gets no expected refusal. Composite, cloned-response, scheme/port, custom-guard, userinfo and boundary fixtures fail respectively on status 307 versus 200 (345/426), missing repeated or rewritten decisions (315/282), and missing attempted-hop decisions (452/477/384/255). Eight shared-primary NeverFollow variants at line 51 plus outer-client line 76, ordinary-client line 93 and Hardening:209 fail the ordinary-follow control with 307 rather than 200 after their restricted-client assertions pass. The unsupported-scheme fixture is the one secondary non-assertion failure: it raises HttpRequestException/SocketException at DifferentialHardening:195/330 while trying files.example:21. Its ConnectCallback explicitly maps every requested host to loopback, so the removed scheme-filtering follower explains an inappropriate local port-21 connection attempt, not an unexplained remote-network outage. Acceptance is independently anchored by the intended decision assertion and the other relevant runtime assertions.

observation_limits: Actual server-hop timing/count assertions use a hermetic loopback server and host-labelled requests, not external host traffic. The two observed requests in the enforcing fixture establish a late refusal after its second loopback send.

NeverFollow shared-primary failures occur in ordinary-follow controls after restricted no-follow assertions pass; do not describe those rows as restricted-policy bypasses. Missing O2 records likewise follow successful no-send assertions.

reviews.rationale: All seven failures detect bypassing restoration of a guard removed from the additional-handler list. The intended Clear fixture reaches Twin:231 and finds zero EgressGuardHandler instances instead of one. Two Hardening:74 variants find no removal warning where one is required. Four NeverFollow variants with clearHandlers=true, across both registration orders and sync/async sends, fail at line 45: the restricted client returns 200 instead of 307. Returning before guard reinsertion also skips assigning the request's NeverFollowRedirects flag, so the still-installed follower does not receive that request policy. This provides a controlled-handler behavioral consequence alongside the runtime chain and diagnostic-count assertions.

reviews.rationale: All 63 failures are causally consistent with forgetting the remembered original redirect setting: the first ReadAndDisable turns known primary auto-follow off, and the added second read captures that disabled value for the follower. The intended Hardening:30 assertion finds firstFollower.Follows=false after primary.AllowAutoRedirect=false passed. Nineteen real loopback differential rows at line 76 show missing normal landings and initial redirect status/final URI/method instead of the reference outcome, including redirect-limit observations. Six method/body twin variants (301 POST, 302 POST, 303 POST, 303 HEAD, 307 POST, 308 POST) raise Sequence contains no matching element at Twin:390 because no /done landing exists; that source line selects the landing before any later method/body comparison. A separate authorization fixture fails ContainSingle at Twin:362 for the same missing landing. Twin:451 retains /r/302#section instead of /done#section, and Twin:415 fails the first relative-redirect status comparison. Other same/cross-host, composite, intermediate-disposal, allowed-boundary and ordinary shared-primary controls return the initial 3xx instead of 200 (Twin:68/89/154/178; Hardening:345/554/426/209; NeverFollow:51/76/93; Differential:97/179). Eight O2 variants at Hardening:384, the loopback O2 case at Differential:255, and custom-guard/userinfo fixtures at Hardening:452/477 lack attempted-hop records while their earlier no-follow/single-send or empty-server checks pass. Enforcement fixtures at Hardening:144 and Differential:121 do not throw because no redirect is followed at all. The netstandard2.0 fixture reaches line 167 with status 302 instead of 200 after confirming one follower at 166. Thus the broad red set detects overrestriction and missing redirect processing, not a claim that these no-follow outcomes sent a forbidden hop.

row.rationale: All 63 failures are causally consistent with forgetting the remembered original redirect setting: the first ReadAndDisable turns known primary auto-follow off, and the added second read captures that disabled value for the follower. The intended Hardening:30 assertion finds firstFollower.Follows=false after primary.AllowAutoRedirect=false passed. Nineteen real loopback differential rows at line 76 show missing normal landings and initial redirect status/final URI/method instead of the reference outcome, including redirect-limit observations. Six method/body twin variants (301 POST, 302 POST, 303 POST, 303 HEAD, 307 POST, 308 POST) raise Sequence contains no matching element at Twin:390 because no /done landing exists; that source line selects the landing before any later method/body comparison. A separate authorization fixture fails ContainSingle at Twin:362 for the same missing landing. Twin:451 retains /r/302#section instead of /done#section, and Twin:415 fails the first relative-redirect status comparison. Other same/cross-host, composite, intermediate-disposal, allowed-boundary and ordinary shared-primary controls return the initial 3xx instead of 200 (Twin:68/89/154/178; Hardening:345/554/426/209; NeverFollow:51/76/93; Differential:97/179). Eight O2 variants at Hardening:384, the loopback O2 case at Differential:255, and custom-guard/userinfo fixtures at Hardening:452/477 lack attempted-hop records while their earlier no-follow/single-send or empty-server checks pass. Enforcement fixtures at Hardening:144 and Differential:121 do not throw because no redirect is followed at all. The netstandard2.0 fixture reaches line 167 with status 302 instead of 200 after confirming one follower at 166. Thus the broad red set detects overrestriction and missing redirect processing, not a claim that these no-follow outcomes sent a forbidden hop.

reviews.rationale: Accepted runtime discovery kill: the exact-type guard excludes derived HttpClientHandler instances, preventing Ashlar from taking ownership of their redirect behavior. All 33 failures are causally consistent. Ten never-follow/shared-primary cases fail ordinary follow controls at NeverFollowTests lines 51, 76 or 93 with 307 rather than 200 after earlier restricted-request controls pass. Four twin decision-record assertions at lines 70, 90, 155 and 180 lose the second decision; two P2 status assertions at 107 and 127 instead receive 200. Eight host-boundary theory cases pass 307 and single-send controls but lose attempted-hop records at HardeningTests line 384. Seven other hardening failures show absent refusal at 144, stopped shared P1 at 209, stopped composite tail at 345, stopped within/outbound redirect at 426, absent second guard decision at 452, missing userinfo-hop record at 477, and unfollowed intermediate 302 at 554. The netstandard harness has the expected follower count but remains at 302 at line 167. The real-loopback differential case passes 307 and empty-server assertions, then lacks the attempted-hop record at line 255. Thus every extra red is explained by the changed recognition predicate, not arbitrary test breakage.

row.rationale: Accepted runtime discovery kill: the exact-type guard excludes derived HttpClientHandler instances, preventing Ashlar from taking ownership of their redirect behavior. All 33 failures are causally consistent. Ten never-follow/shared-primary cases fail ordinary follow controls at NeverFollowTests lines 51, 76 or 93 with 307 rather than 200 after earlier restricted-request controls pass. Four twin decision-record assertions at lines 70, 90, 155 and 180 lose the second decision; two P2 status assertions at 107 and 127 instead receive 200. Eight host-boundary theory cases pass 307 and single-send controls but lose attempted-hop records at HardeningTests line 384. Seven other hardening failures show absent refusal at 144, stopped shared P1 at 209, stopped composite tail at 345, stopped within/outbound redirect at 426, absent second guard decision at 452, missing userinfo-hop record at 477, and unfollowed intermediate 302 at 554. The netstandard harness has the expected follower count but remains at 302 at line 167. The real-loopback differential case passes 307 and empty-server assertions, then lacks the attempted-hop record at line 255. Thus every extra red is explained by the changed recognition predicate, not arbitrary test breakage.

row.rationale: Accepted runtime boundary kill: adding MaxAutomaticRedirections < 0 makes the outside-to-host-boundary stop ineffective. All nine actual failures are explained. Six HTTP theory variants (IPv4 and IPv6 loopback, localhost, svc.localhost and both link-local addresses) return 200 instead of 307 at HardeningTests line 381. The unix and npipe variants retain 307 and one stub send, then lack the attempted-hop record at line 384. The differential RemoteFrontedPrimary to SocketsHttpHandler to loopback Kestrel path returns 200 instead of 307 at DifferentialHardeningTests line 253. The latter is a real loopback redirect-response observation tied to the disabled boundary stop.

reviews.rationale: Accepted runtime client-specific policy kill: removing the EgressNoFollowClient singleton drops the request marker required to restrict existing shared followers. All eight Never_follow_wins theory combinations return 200 rather than 307 at NeverFollowTests line 45; the outer shared-follower case returns 200 rather than 307 at line 72. The started real-primary differential case completes its restricted request but returns 200 rather than 302 at DifferentialHardeningTests line 176. Its successful warmup and disabled-setting assertions at 169-170 precede the failing restricted status.

row.rationale: Accepted from all 16 actual runtime failures. The exact loop mutation in EgressRefusal.Find visits only aggregate child0; the test wrapper puts an unrelated exception in child0 and nests the refusal in child1. Three unkeyed DI/router rows fail their first identity assertion at EgressRefusalPropagationTests line 49: stages0/1 retain HttpRequestException("wrapper-canary"), while stage3 ends with InvalidOperationException("dispose-canary"). All ten direct auditing rows (stages0-4 by auditThrows false/true) fail identity at 153. Seven retain the wrapper: stage0/false and both variants of stages1,2,4. Stage0/true instead exposes audit-canary because missing refusal detection selects ordinary fault emission at AuditingChatClient line 67, whose auditor throws. Both stage3 variants expose dispose-canary because activeRefusal remains unset and the disposal protection at line 168 cannot apply; in stage3/true disposal can also supersede the auditor exception. Two wrapped echo rows, deterministic true/false, fail identity at test113 with actual null because ThrowIfPresent misses the refusal and fallback returns. The classifier row fails124 because wrapped-refusal classification becomes true, after direct-refusal false at123 passes. All extra failures therefore follow from the omitted aggregate branch, including the changed audit/disposal exception identities. Five controls pass: both direct-refusal echo rows, both direct guard-refusal DI rows and reference formatting.

Four actual main-theory rows (stage1 False, stage2 True, stage1 True, stage2 False in TRX order) fail identity assertion EgressRefusalPropagationTests.cs:153, observing HttpRequestException wrapper-canary instead of the embedded refusal. Actual stacks identify RefusingClient.GetStreamingResponseAsync199 for stage1 and GetAsyncEnumerator201 for stage2, followed by product89/181. The nonempty wrapper fails the new condition, so activeRefusal assignment94, EmitRefusal96 and ThrowIfPresent97 are skipped. Enumerator assignment does not complete; the finally has no enumerator to dispose. Both audit settings consequently expose the wrapper along these fixture paths; all 21 rows pass after restoration.
